sources.citation: OLAC 'Resources in and about the Burumakok language' (Internet Archive copy 2023-10-03)
sources.note: Lists only Glottolog, Ethnologue and LINGUIST List records; no archival deposits, no descriptions.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid buru1307 reference list (Wilbrink 2004; van den Heuvel & Fedden 2014; Campbell et al. 2022 ELCat) and Wikipedia 'Burumakok language'
sources.note: Nothing on stress; confirms no grammar/phonology exists for Burumakok. transnewguinea.org has no Burumakok entry (API checked, 1081 languages).

sources.citation: van den Heuvel, Wilco & Sebastian Fedden. 2014. Greater Awyu and Greater Ok: inheritance or contact? Oceanic Linguistics 53(1): 1-36. (JSTOR scan deposited on HAL hal-03950196)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level remark only (p.2, scanned of page image): 'While Mountain Ok languages are described as tonal (Telefol, Tifal, Mian), in Lowland Ok and Greater Awyu languages it is not the tone contour but lexical stress that seems to be distinctive.' Burumakok, Kopkaka and Kwer are not mentioned anywhere in the paper (checked text layer of all 37 pp. and scanned of pp. 3-8); their 'Lowland Ok' follows Healey 1964 (Ngalum, Kati/Muyu, Ninggerum, Yonggom), so the remark does not clearly cover Burumakok.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens, Ruth Wester & Wilco van den Heuvel. 2012. The Greater Awyu language family of West Papua. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia Special Issue 2012 (Part I): 269-312.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Burumakok (not mentioned); uses Kopkaka morphology from Kroneman 2010 (unpublished Kopkaka grammar sketch). Silent on stress for the Kwer-Kopkaka-Burumakok group.

sources.citation: Hughes, Jock. 2009. Upper Digul Survey. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2009-003 (10 pp; downloaded from the Internet Archive, kept in scratch only)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Does not cover Burumakok (Korowai, Tsaukambo-Komyandaret, Wanggom, Tangko, Nakai, Wambon only).

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. Newguineaworld: 'West Ok' and 'Kopkaka' pages (source inventories). newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; phonology sections 'under construction'. Lists the only Burumakok material as Wilbrink (2004) '239+ comparative terms for Burumakok, Kwer, Tokuni, and Marub' and '(pp. 109a-109f) Buramakok and Kwer villages after Mark Donohue'; Wilbrink 2004:29-58 is a phonology of Kopkaka (Seradela), not Burumakok.

sources.citation: Kroneman, Dick. 2010. Kopkaka grammar sketch. Unpublished manuscript (cited in de Vries, Wester & van den Heuvel 2012 and on Newguineaworld).

sources.note: Nearest described relative (Kopkaka, kopk1238, same Kwer-Kopkaka-Burumakok branch); would give the only stress statement for the branch, though not for Burumakok itself.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. n.d. Field wordlists of Burumakok and Kwer (unpublished; reproduced in Wilbrink 2004 appendices).

sources.note: Donohue's phonetic transcriptions typically mark stress/tone; the raw list would be the only phonetic record of Burumakok prosody.

sources.citation: Wilbrink, Ans. 2004. The Kopkaka of Papua. Provisional notes on their language, its language affiliation and on the Kopkaka culture. Amsterdam: Vrije Universiteit (219 pp; Appendices pp. 97-219 with Burumakok comparative wordlist and a Burumakok list 'after Mark Donohue', pp. 109a-109f).

sources.note: The only primary material on Burumakok known to Glottolog/Usher; the wordlist transcriptions may carry stress marks, and the Kopkaka phonology chapter (pp. 29-58) may comment on stress in the closely related West Ok lects. Not found online (VU thesis/report).
